summary: Richard Hauschild worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Leipzig under Johannes Hertel, and Jena under Albert Debrunner. He held posts as Lektor at the University of Jena (1938) and ordentliches Mitglied at the Saxon Academy of Sciences (1949–1972).

Richard Henebry was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's College, Maynooth, Greifswald, and Freiburg. He also studied under Heinrich Zimmer between approximately 1896 and 1898.

Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees from Alberta, SOAS, and London under Arthur Waley, David Friedman, David Snellgrove, and Edward Conze. He taught at Toronto (1954) and became Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994–2014).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving notably as a psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994–2019) and on the faculty at the Graduate Theological Union (~1995).

Richard Keith Sprigg was a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. After attending Oakham School (~1936–1940), he held appointments at the University of London and SOAS University of London from approximately 1948 to 1980.

Kieckhefer studied history and religion at Saint Louis University, UT Austin, and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. In 1975 he became Professor of History and Religious Studies at Northwestern University, later serving as president of Societas Magica and the American Society of Church History.

King is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster, and under Daniel Mariau. He held posts at Stirling (~1996–2002), Vanderbilt (~2002–2007), and the University of Glasgow (~2008–2011).
Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1995–1999) and Duke University (~1999).

Richard Mahoney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under the supervision of Paul Harrison and was also affiliated with the university in 2001.

Richard Morris worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Battersea. He served as Winchester lecturer at King's College School (1869), headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888), and master at Dedham Grammar School (~1875–1892).

Richard P. Boyle conducted graduate studies at the University of Washington and studied under traditional teacher Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was affiliated with the University of New Mexico in 2015.

Hayes specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, also studying under Shoryu Katsura and T. Venkatacharya. He taught at Toronto, McGill (attested 1997–2009), and New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).
Richard Peter Hottelet was active in Buddhist studies. In 1971, he was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani.

Richard Phené Spiers was active in history and archaeology. He pursued his education at King's College London from approximately 1856 to 1858 and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts from around 1858 to 1861.

Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held chairs at Kiel (1875), Halle (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908), and served as administrator and librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Historian Richard Polenberg earned degrees from Brooklyn College (~1955–1959) and Columbia University (~1959–1964). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University (1966–2011) and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1974–1975).

Philosopher Richard Rorty studied at Chicago and Yale (PhD 1952–1956). He held posts at Wellesley (1958–1961), Princeton (~1962–1982), the University of Virginia as Kenan Professor of Humanities (1982–1998), and Stanford (1998).
